questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L02_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.SIM.2

Which transformation changes size but preserves shape?

feedback.text: A dilation changes size by a scale factor while preserving shape.
A translation preserves both size and shape.
A reflection preserves size and shape.
A rotation preserves size and shape.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L02_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.SIM.2

A dilation has scale factor 2. What similarity conclusion is supported?

answer.text: The image is congruent to the preimage.

feedback.text: Congruence would require the same size.

answer.text: The image is similar to the preimage.

feedback.text: A dilation preserves shape and changes size, so it supports similarity.
Dilation preserves angle measures.
The figures can be compared through the dilation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L02_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.3

A sequence says reflect, then dilate. What happens first?

feedback.text: Dilate happens after reflect in this sequence.
Translation is not named.
Transformation sequences are performed in the order given.
Rotation is not named.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L02_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.4

A figure maps onto itself after a 180° turn. What symmetry is shown?

feedback.text: Reflection symmetry uses a mirror line.
Translation symmetry uses a slide.
The mapping onto itself shows symmetry.
A turn that maps a figure onto itself is rotation symmetry.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L02_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.4

A line divides a figure into matching mirror halves. What symmetry is shown?

feedback.text: A mirror line shows reflection symmetry.
Rotation symmetry requires a turn.
Translation symmetry requires a slide.
Dilation changes size and is not this symmetry.
